phases.objective: Provide deployment-owned Production Recovery approval and execution-ticket authority primitives over the existing independent Recovery Control Store without creating a complete live graph or touching Production.

e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: A server-owned canary foundation exposes durable approval/ticket/deployment-identity authorities while declaring all consequential executor/readback/ledger components deferred and production_live disabled.
steps: Create a dedicated Ed25519 execution-ticket signer and verifier without returning private material.
Construct the Recovery Control Store through an injected factory and require exact verifier object identity.
Derive approval material server-side from the immutable challenge binding without persisting or returning the token.
Persist bounded challenge references only through the independent Recovery Control Store.
Wrap the server-derived Production deployment attestation source.
Return the six deferred consequential components explicitly and keep activation ineligible.
assertions: No database connection, provider access, workflow dispatch, migration, grant, deployment or Production mutation occurs during foundation construction.
Approval material is not persisted and is never returned by challenge issuance.
Recovery Store execution-ticket verifier object identity exactly matches the signer authority's verifier.
Wrong ticket hashes and approval material fail verification.
The foundation reports complete_authority_graph=false, production_live_enabled=false and activation_eligible=false.
Mutation executor, Hostinger executor, independent readback, partial receipts, proof resolver and migration ledger remain explicit blockers.

phases.objective: Keep Production live Recovery blocked until all deferred authorities, fresh signed certification, exact deployment attestation and separate activation authorization exist.
